title: Should decade's side of the protocol be public in decade-channel?
body:
`decade-channel` exports types that only decade's server builds: `Reply`, the enum decade writes for each answer, and `Captured`, the base64 PNG inside `Reply::Screenshot`. decade uses them in `decade/src/server/channel.rs` and `decade/src/server/compositor/channels.rs`, so the server and the client share one definition of the wire. A client never needs them. Adding a variant to `Reply` is a breaking change to `decade-channel` even though clients do not use it.

## Options

- Keep them public, and mark `Reply` and `Message` `#[non_exhaustive]` so new variants stop breaking clients.
- Move the shared wire types into a crate both depend on, and keep `decade-channel` to the client's API.
- Hide them behind a cargo feature that only decade turns on.
